evidence.detail: normalize_version() patterns list: pattern 2 is r'(\s)[\[({]?(\d[\.\.\d]*)[])}]?$' — requires a space before the number; 'RealRhinos1.0' has no space so it is never normalized
Test case: ('FDSe 1.0', 'FDSe v1') works because of the space; no test case for attached dotted versions like 'RealRhinos1.0'

Existing guard: names with digits separated by letters are left unchanged, protecting '2 combos are better than 1'; this guard does NOT apply to 'RealRhinos1.0' since only '.' (not a letter) separates the two digits
is_semver() correctly rejects date-like numbers (12.30) and price-like numbers (0.02), so a new pattern for dotted versions can safely reuse the same guard

triage.fix_sketch: In decksite/deck_name.py add a fourth pattern to the patterns list at line 302: r'()(\ d\.\ d[\.\d]*)$' (captures an empty group as spacer and a dotted number at end-of-name, without requiring a preceding space). The existing spacer logic (line 314: spacer=' ' when group(1)!='-') correctly inserts a space, giving 'RealRhinos v1'. Add test cases in decksite/deck_name_test.py: ('RealRhinos1.0', 'RealRhinos v1') and verify ('RDW23', 'Rdw23') still passes (RDW23 has no dot so the new pattern does not match). ~10 lines changed.
triage.notes: The 'can we get there without breaking other things?' framing is addressable: plain integers attached to words (e.g. RDW23) are safe because the pattern requires at least one dot (\d\.\d); date-like and price-like dotted numbers are filtered by the existing is_semver() check. Existing tests provide good regression coverage.
